checked_sources.evidence: Opened official Octans boundary-coordinate table; supports the constellation-region distinction.

2024 original traceback study gives Octans at about 150 pc, declinations −86° to −20°, Gaia DR3 plus radial velocities, and 34+2/−2 Myr as its most precise dynamical age; explains traceback as closest past orbital convergence.
Original low-mass-member spectroscopy finds 29 K5–M4 candidates, Li I in nine, and a 30–40 Myr lithium age with constrained membership/age.
Opened official Piscis Austrinus boundary-coordinate table.

NASA reports Fomalhaut in Piscis Austrinus, MIRI’s three nested belts extending 23 billion km, previously unresolved inner belts, collision debris, and the original possible collision-cloud interpretation.
Original JWST/MIRI paper supports the spatially resolved debris-disk structures and the cautious possible dust-collision interpretation.
Original ALMA/Keck follow-up concludes the Great Dust Cloud is a background object rather than a common-proper-motion companion/system component.

Original 2025 study uses Gemini GHOST systemic radial velocity and Gaia cluster velocity; it concludes NGC 2818/NGC 2818A are physically associated while accurately noting prior debate, and says the PN phase is typically tens of thousands of years.
NASA identifies NGC 2818 and NGC 2818A together in Pyxis and describes the rare nebula–open-cluster context.
Opened official Triangulum Australe boundary-coordinate table; NGC 6025 J2000 center in the cited photometric paper lies within it.

Original 2006 abstract states five-year repeated observations of 78 stars across NGC 6025 and Blanco 1; in NGC 6025 it finds two double-lined binaries, one kinematic non-member, and eight variable/asymmetric-line candidates with rotation/spots/pulsation caveats.
Original photometric work lists NGC 6025 coordinates (16:03:17, −60:25:54) and supports its open-cluster context for the IAU-boundary comparison.
